description: Four complaints covering the correlation tiers. The first names a transaction reference, which is a tier-1 identity and needs no confidence score. The last names nothing specific and should correlate weakly or not at all.

records.narrative_raw: I transferred Rs 24,000 to what I believed was a verified seller. The reference on my statement is TXN-S-FANIN-01. The seller stopped responding immediately afterwards.

metadata_json.tier: 1 -- exact transaction reference. Deterministic: no confidence, no review state, because this is an identity rather than an inference.

records.narrative_raw: Paid for a phone that never arrived. I do not have the transaction number but it was the same afternoon and the amount was about twenty four thousand rupees.

metadata_json.tier: 2 -- named suspect account, no reference. Still deterministic, because the complainant named the account.

records.narrative_raw: Received a message claiming to be from my bank and entered my details. Money left my account within the hour.

metadata_json.tier: 3 to 5 -- inferred. Matched on amount and timing rather than on an identifier, so it carries a confidence score and a review state, and a person decides whether to accept it.

records.narrative_raw: Someone has been using my details. I am not sure which transactions are affected or when it started.

metadata_json.note: Deliberately vague. It should correlate weakly or not at all. A correlation engine that finds a confident match here is matching noise, and the review queue is where that becomes somebody's wasted afternoon.
